## TrailFold Daypack 18L — Static Meta Creative Production Brief

**Objective:** Produce three 4:5 static-feed concepts that clarify the most relevant purchase questions: daily commute use, laptop compatibility, and a practical commute-to-short-trip use case. Use plain-spoken copy. These are **drafts**, not live ads.

**Inventory guardrail:** Daypack stock is 210 units against current average sales of 8/day; confirmed replenishment arrives in 35 days. Do not scale a winning Daypack ad without confirming the live inventory forecast. Keep this as a controlled creative read, not a volume-growth push.

### Concept 1 — Desk-to-trail iteration
**Hypothesis:** Showing the same bag in a work setting and an outdoor setting will make the Daypack’s intended commute-plus-short-trip role immediately clear.

- **Headline:** From commute to weekend
- **Primary body:** A practical 18L daypack for workdays, day trips, and short weekends. Includes a padded sleeve for laptops up to 13 inches and an external bottle pocket.
- **CTA:** Shop Daypack 18L
- **Image composition:** One continuous, believable scene split by use rather than a hard graphic divide. Left: bag beside a desk, with a closed laptop nearby. Right: the same bag outdoors on a simple day-trip setting. Keep the bag large and readable in both halves. Add only one small overlay: “18L / laptop sleeve / bottle pocket.”
- **Production instructions:** Use the product on-body or in context rather than a plain-background packshot. Keep background uncluttered, natural light, no destination or performance claims. Do not show the bag in heavy rain or imply it is waterproof. Make a 4:5 master (1080×1350); leave top and bottom safe space for placement crops.

### Concept 2 — Laptop-fit objection
**Hypothesis:** Directly stating the 13-inch laptop limit will qualify shoppers and reduce uncertainty without making an unsupported claim about 15-inch devices.

- **Headline:** Built for laptops up to 13 inches
- **Primary body:** The Daypack 18L has a padded laptop sleeve designed for laptops up to 13 inches. For a larger device, check your laptop dimensions before ordering.
- **CTA:** Check the details
- **Image composition:** Open-bag product view with a clearly sized 13-inch laptop being placed into, or visible in, the padded sleeve. Use a clean callout pointing to the sleeve: “Padded sleeve: up to 13-inch laptop.”
- **Production instructions:** The laptop should read as 13-inch through prop selection or a discreet “13-inch” label; do not use visual tricks that suggest a 15-inch laptop fits. No comparison chart, competitor bag, or “fits most laptops” language. Keep the product and sleeve opening fully visible; avoid covering the key proof point with text.

### Concept 3 — Fresh positioning: pack less, carry one bag
**Hypothesis:** A restrained “one practical bag” message will resonate with commuters who take short trips, without relying on adventure-led imagery.

- **Headline:** One bag for the week and the weekend
- **Primary body:** The Daypack 18L keeps the essentials close: a padded 13-inch laptop sleeve, external bottle pocket, and water-resistant fabric for everyday use. Water-resistant, not waterproof.
- **CTA:** See the Daypack
- **Image composition:** Flat-lay or open-bag overhead shot showing a modest, realistic mix of commute and short-trip essentials around the bag: closed laptop, charging cable, bottle, light layer, and small personal items. The bag remains the focal point. Overlay: “18L. Practical by design.”
- **Production instructions:** Do not overstuff the bag or imply a specific packing capacity beyond 18L. Keep the layout spare and functional, not aspirational travel imagery. Show water resistance only in copy; do not show rain, puddles, or submerged product.

## Single-variable test plan
Run all three drafts plus the current desk-to-trail creative as four ads in **one existing Daypack prospecting ad set**. The single variable is the **creative package** (static image and its paired copy). Hold audience, optimization event, placements, bid strategy, landing page, and attribution setting constant. Use equal starting delivery where platform controls allow; do not make mid-test edits. Use a capped draft test allocation of **$900 total** ($225 per ad) and review only after each ad has comparable spend. Evaluate Shopify orders and Daypack stock alongside Meta delivery; treat Meta reported purchase value as directional because it is not reconciled to Shopify. Pause the test if inventory forecasting indicates stockout before replenishment arrival.

**Acceptance checklist:** 4:5 master delivered for each concept; editable source file; copy applied exactly as above; no testimonials, competitor references, waterproof language, unverified durability claims, or 15-inch fit implication.

task.title: Agency creative production brief
task.request: Create three distinct static Meta ad briefs for Daypack: one iteration of desk-to-trail, one laptop-fit objection concept and one fresh positioning hypothesis. Give actual headline/body/CTA, image composition, production instructions and a single-variable test plan. Allocate no more than 8 designer hours total.
